Kim and Nancy arrive at Sasaki Shuzō in Nishijin with a month of reading behind them and a question about water. What they get is a tour of the well, the milled rice, the mold room and the cold tanks, and then a tasting designed like an experiment: three sakes identical in every way but how they left the mash. Real people, real place, real bottles; the dialogue is what the day would have sounded like. Twenty-two photographs and eleven small infographics on how sake is made and what "quality" measures.
